blocks.text: MAT:200–222 DETAILED REVIEW AND DELEGATED APPROVAL — CANONICAL

The packet compared four genuinely different candidates per address, scored 36 candidates, supplied tailored runtime-state and lexical-trit distinctions, audited eleven competing families, and ran 85 unique English Matter concept tests. The pre-approval gate passed 21 checks and all 2,592 deterministic generation assertions. A separate post-migration validation passed 17 checks.
MAT:200 — enduring physical work capacity — A persistent capacity of a material bearer to supply energy for producing physical change.
MAT:201 — available physical work capacity — A material bearer’s capacity to supply energy for physical change that is presently available for exercise.
MAT:202 — latent physical work capacity — A material bearer’s capacity to supply energy for physical change that exists without being presently available for exercise.
MAT:210 — established material coupling — An established relation by which a material bearer can transmit physical influence to a distinct target.
MAT:211 — active material coupling — A relation by which a material bearer is presently transmitting physical influence to a distinct target.
MAT:212 — unresolved material coupling — Whether a material bearer can transmit physical influence to a distinct target is unresolved.
MAT:220 — established systemic material interdependence — A stable relation in which material parts of a shared system mutually constrain one another’s physical states.
MAT:221 — active systemic material interdependence — A relation in which material parts of a shared system are presently exerting reciprocal physical influence.
MAT:222 — potential systemic material interdependence — An unrealized possible relation in which material parts of a shared system would mutually constrain one another’s physical states.

Design boundary: MAT:2xx now forms one material-influence architecture. The inward triplet owns physical work capacity; the outward triplet owns directed material coupling; the systemic triplet owns mutual physical interdependence. Structure and topology remain STR; ownership and access remain CON; quantities and formal constraints remain LOG or quantity grammar; conservation law remains ORI/LOG; damage, repair, design, movement, and material-change events remain in their own families or canonical MAT/MOV layers.
